body.statement: There is a deterministic Turing-model algorithm that, for every input in \(\mathfrak C_k\), outputs every coefficient of every \(F_{\ell,A}(z)\) with \(|A|\le2\) and, under nondegenerate isolation, every entry of every \(Q_{\ell}\), using \(Ln^2 2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations. The algorithm contains no table of size \((nb)^k\), no unevaluated integral, and every intermediate rational has \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit length.
body.justification: The theorem turns a simulation-chosen network design into an exactly evaluable rule library on a broad cyclic graph class.
body.gap: Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li simulate a surrogate; random sequential adsorption gives scalar tree occupation; static independent-set algorithms omit greedy-order probabilities. None supplies this exact feedback-core oracle.
body.consumer: After measuring the feedback number, investigators can compare candidate AWRI priority rules before a rural-China insurance-diffusion follow-up.
